messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Runtime pool r-03 p99 latency spike (x4) + 5xx rate ~2.3% after staged rollout 2026-03-14T11:22Z; paging oncall. Trigger: canary health checks tripped.
jamie: i'm awake, grabbing logs/trace. which rollout id?
sasha: looks like rollout r-20260314-11. we’re seeing kernel fallback on a subset of hosts + KV pool growth. batching queues are backing up.
mira: customer-impact: Hosted API customers in eu-central seeing increased timeouts and some requests 504/502. support already getting tickets.
lucas: early hypothesis: new dynamic-concurrency-v2 heuristic increased per-worker concurrency causing kv allocator pressure -> evictions -> kernel fallback under long sequences.
jamie: can we flip the kill-switch for dynamic-concurrency-v2 while we triage? want a fast mitigation.
taylor: +1, flip it to false for r-03 canary group. I can run the flag toggle.
jamie: executing now: ```bash
# toggle feature flag for rollout r-20260314-11 canary
redwood-ctl rollout feature-flag set r-20260314-11 dynamic-concurrency-v2 false --targets=pool:r-03-canary
```
incident-bot: deploy-bot: feature flag update accepted, change-id ffu-2945009876 queued.
taylor: applied. monitoring…
sasha: seeing immediate reduction in evictions on the affected nodes. p99 trending down but still ~1.6x baseline. errors dropped from 2.3% -> 0.9%.
mira: opened incident on status.redwood.ai: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-29450 - posting to customers in affected regions now.
lucas: recommend full rollback of the staged rollout (not just flag) if stabilization not complete in 15m. we should avoid manual kernel-level fiddling.
jamie: starting rollback to previous revision r-20260314-09 now. command: ```bash
redwood-ctl rollout undo r-20260314-11 --to-revision r-20260314-09 --targets=pool:r-03
```
incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated, progress: 0% -> 40% (nodes draining)
taylor: note: draining will evict KV entries briefly; we should watch prefetch hit-rate and batch queue depth.
sasha: after rollback progress ~70% p99 down to 1.05x baseline, 5xx ~0.2% — close to normal. kernel fallback traces cleared on previously impacted nodes.
mira: support-nora, please update the incident page and ping top affected customers with current status and ETA for full resolution.
support-nora: updating now, message drafted: "We're seeing reduced errors after rollback; investigating root cause; ETA for full resolution 30m." posting.
jamie: rollback completed. systems stable on r-03. handing off to mira for postmortem and RCA.
mira: taking over for postmortem. immediate follow-ups: 1) revert dynamic-concurrency-v2 in main branch until perf tests cover long seq cases; 2) add KV pool saturation alert; 3) add canary smoke that simulates long-sequence tails; 4) include batching/kv interactions in checklist before rollout.
lucas: i'll prepare a reproducer and perf test harness. also propose a short-term mitigation: throttle per-worker concurrency by sequence-length buckets.
taylor: noted for next hotfix. if anyone else needs handoff: jamie -> mira (oncall handover).
jamie: small log snippet we saw before kill-switch: ```json
{"node":"r-03-17","evictions":1423,"kernel_fallback":true,"batch_queue_len":384}
```
sasha: adding: trace id t-9b7f shows repeated kernel fallback on repeated long-token sequences from a small set of customers. might be traffic pattern sensitive.
mira: assigning owners for follow-ups: lucas (perf reproducer), sasha (alerts + tracing), jamie (deploy checklist), taylor (feature rollout gating). I'll schedule a 1hr postmortem in #eng-runtime.
support-nora: customers notified, status page updated to "Investigating -> Identified -> Monitoring".
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: metrics stabilized, follow-ups assigned. Remember to file full postmortem within 72h. :white_check_mark:
jamie: thanks all, nice rapid response.
mira: thanks team, taking it from here. please drop any stray notes in the postmortem doc.
